meta.title: Joona Lipponen – running for Chair of SYL 2027
meta.description: Joona Lipponen, Chair of the AYY Board, is running for Chair of SYL for 2027. The vision: impactful direction and collaborative advocacy.

hero.name: Joona Lipponen
facts: Master's student in real estate economics

image.alt: Joona sits on a wooden chair and smiles

hero.cta: At the General Assembly on 13–14 November, you can say “yo to yoona”.

vision.heading: Goals
vision.intro: SYL does a lot of good work, but it isn't always visible in the field. Next year will decide whether students' goals make it into the Government Programme. That's why I'm running for Chair.

goals.title: Achieving students' parliamentary election goals together
goals.text: Next year's goal is clear: to get students' parliamentary election goals into the Government Programme. We'll do it through solution-oriented dialogue with decision-makers!

goals.title: Putting student unions' voices at the heart of SYL's work
goals.text: We will strengthen student unions' opportunities to take part in planning SYL's activities and advocacy work. SYL must not end up in its own bubble.

goals.title: Students as builders of Finland's future
goals.text: We will bring students into public debate more boldly and in more diverse ways by showing why investing in students pays off.

vision.pull: The foundation is good. The execution can be sharper.

proof.title: Example: housing
proof.text: Funding for student housing affects every student union. When the student movement speaks about it with one voice, from Rovaniemi to Jyväskylä and Lappeenranta, it is heard all the way to Parliament.

vision.statement: My vision for SYL is **impactful direction and collaborative advocacy**
vision.goalsIntro: To make this vision happen, I've set three goals for my year as Chair.

promises.heading: Promises to the field
promises.intro: Concrete things you can follow up on.
items: A one-hour call with the chair of every student union, twice a year.
Transparency: the field always knows what SYL is doing and why.

about.heading: About me
paragraphs: I'm Joona, 27, and this year I'm Chair of the Board of the Aalto University Student Union AYY. Alongside that, I'm doing my master's in real estate economics in Aalto's Urban Studies and Planning programme. As a candidate not affiliated with any political party, I want to represent all students and get people from different backgrounds working towards common goals!
I found my way into student organisations through Otaniemi in 2020: first as a tutor, then as my guild's fuksicaptain and as head judge of the Jäynä competition.
In 2024, as the AYY Board member responsible for housing and finance, I found my passion for societal advocacy, because student housing determines who can afford to study.
At AYY I've seen that advocacy works when the field knows what's being done and gets to take part before decisions are made. That's what I want to bring to SYL.

image.alt: Joona in a teekkari cap and overalls in Otaniemi in 2022

timeline.heading: The road here

items.title: Starting at Aalto
items.text: Otaniemi sweeps me along, studies begin.

items.title: Tutor and outreach lead
items.text: Supporting new students. As outreach lead, I led a group that promoted our field to upper secondary students.

items.title: Guild fuksicaptain
items.text: Responsible for welcoming new students to Aalto.

items.title: Head judge of the Jäynä competition
items.text: For a year, I led a group of volunteer friends whose task is to keep the jäynä prank culture alive and organise the competition.

items.title: Chair of the AYY Board
items.text: Leading the student union between the office and the Representative Council.

image.alt: Joona speaking as Chair of AYY at Aalto University's academic year opening

items.title: Running for Chair of SYL
items.text: The election takes place at the General Assembly on 13–14 November 2026.

timeline.note: Plus many other volunteer roles in the Otaniemi student community, such as student representative in my school's EDI group.

items.text: I brought fees for student representatives in university administration to the Aalto Board. They were approved.
The employment voucher for international students is moving forward to a study by the City of Espoo.

items.big: Change management after shutting down Trinet
items.text: I led the change management after AYY's 40-year-old student network was shut down. The difficult decision led to a member vote and sparked a lot of discussion, which divided the community. Under my Board's leadership, we rebuilt trust and unity so that the community was brought back together before the start of the next academic year.

items.big: Summer job campaign with Aalto University
items.text: In our member survey, employment came up as students' biggest concern. We raised the issue with the university's leadership, and now we're building a corporate social responsibility campaign together with Aalto that encourages companies to offer students summer jobs.

attitude.heading: With what attitude
attitude.intro: In volunteer work, no one is obliged to do anything. That's why, for me, leadership is above all about helping people see why something is worth doing.

items.title: Without the stick
items.text: Motivation comes from people understanding the goal and seeing their own part in it. Orders won't get you far in volunteer work.

items.title: All perspectives on the table
items.text: I create a space where even difficult things can be discussed before decisions are made. Disagreement during preparation costs less than after the decision.

items.title: Between the office and the Council
items.text: As Chair of AYY, I've led work between the professional staff and elected officials. Both need to pull in the same direction.

references.heading: Recommendations
references.note: The recommendations have been translated from Finnish.

positions.heading: Positions
positions.intro: Answers to questions I've been asked. I'll add more as the campaign goes on.

items.q: How do we solve the student housing shortage?
items.a: By building. Construction of student housing has slowed down because state investment grants for non-profit student housing have been abolished. They must be restored. Housing is the foundation for being able to study, and its price determines who can afford to study.

items.q: Should university education come with tuition fees?
items.a: Not in any form. Tuition fees create inequality. They also hinder lifelong learning when someone applies for a second degree, and take away young people's chance to try and fail if a field turns out to be the wrong one.

items.q: Should the open university be allowed to award degrees?
items.a: No. The open university pathway was designed for young people who don't yet have a study place, and it should stay that way. A separate new pathway must be developed for adults and lifelong learning.

items.q: Why is investing in students worth it?
items.a: Students are not just an expense. We have solutions to Finland's big questions, and students' issues must be linked to these bigger themes. Education brings growth, international graduates ease the labour shortage, and today's students are building tomorrow's Finland.

items.q: How do we get international students to stay in Finland?
items.a: Through employment. As Chair of AYY, I've pushed the City of Espoo for an employment voucher for international students, and it is now moving forward to a study. The same idea is behind the employer voucher in SYL's parliamentary election programme.
